key_insight: Ti3C2Tx MXene stability in perovskite precursor inks depends on the constituent: iodine species accelerate degradation, while methylammonium iodide helps passivate the surface.
engineering_relevance: Controlling precursor composition and addition sequence can help preserve and tune MXene surfaces for integration into perovskite solar cells.
method: Expose MXenes to individual and combined MAPbI3 precursor components.
Analyze surface chemistry using X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy.
Use density functional theory to investigate constituent–surface interactions.
evidence_signal: Combined XPS and DFT findings indicate rapid oxidation and dissolution with iodine species, slower PbI2-driven oxidation, and hydrogen-bond-mediated stabilization by MAI.
watch_item: The abstract reports chemistry in a model MAPbI3 precursor system, not demonstrated gains in solar-cell efficiency or operational lifetime.
paper_title: Dynamic Chemical Changes of Ti3C2Tx MXenes in Halide Perovskite Precursor Environments
